claims.text: The catalytic performance of a transition-metal catalyst is governed by the oxidation state of its surface sites.
A higher degree of controlled surface oxidation enhances selectivity by tuning reactant adsorption energies.
Pristine platinum or palladium catalysts possess a native surface oxide or hydride layer.
Oxidative versus reductive pretreatment can controllably modify the surface oxidation state.
The surface oxidation state influences the d-band electron density of surface metal atoms.
Changes in d-band electron density alter the adsorption energies of key reactants.
Controlled surface oxidation changes the binding strengths of adsorbed species.
An oxidized surface can favor pathways producing selective partial-oxidation products over complete oxidation or side reactions.
Surface oxidation can improve durability by limiting over-adsorption and subsequent catalyst deactivation.
Oxidatively pretreated catalysts will have a higher fraction of oxidized surface sites than reductively pretreated catalysts.
Oxidatively pretreated catalysts will exhibit higher desired-product selectivity than reductively pretreated catalysts.
Reductively pretreated catalysts may exhibit higher conversion rates than oxidatively pretreated catalysts.
The lower selectivity predicted after reductive pretreatment results from over-adsorption and side reactions.
The proposed relationship should hold under conditions that do not cause significant sintering or structural phase changes.
The proposed relationship is most applicable when adsorption-energy modulation determines the reaction pathway, particularly in selective oxidation or reduction reactions.
The magnitude of activity, selectivity, and durability changes depends on the transition metal, reaction system, and pretreatment parameters.

contradictions.description: An inert atmosphere is grouped with reductive treatment, although inert exposure does not necessarily reduce the surface; the later predictions assume that this group has undergone genuinely reductive pretreatment.
